$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json
through the ts-bridge adaptation, trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here.
Precedent for a per-repo port: kubelab, hive, web and ts-bridge each carry their own copy;
the SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory` (measured 2026-09-06 on master at 6bcb859). Its exit status is non-zero both when
triage is pending AND when the question cannot be computed, so an unanswerable queue is never
mistaken for a clear one; but a check that says the same thing on every run stops being read.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over the comments of the
last 15 PRs (#111..#129) with `gh api repos/mlorentedev/pdf-modifier-mcp/issues/<n>/comments`.
What CodeRabbit actually emits in this repo, by PR:
## Walkthrough            -> #111 #114 #117 #124 #126 #128 #129   (a review ran; the attesting marker)
## Review limit reached   -> #121 #123 #129   (each also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai';
#129 was declined first and reviewed later, so both markers coexist)
No actionable comments were generated in the recent review
-> #114 #126   (only ever alongside ## Walkthrough, never alone, so it
is deliberately NOT listed: Walkthrough already covers those PRs)
## Review skipped         -> never observed in #111..#129; kept in declined_markers because it
is CodeRabbit's documented output for a diff with nothing reviewable
(no CodeRabbit output)    -> #112 #113 #115 #116 #125 (dependabot), #122 (release-please)
CodeRabbit publishes no check-run here: the rollup on #128 is add-to-project, Bandit, GitGuardian,
Gitleaks, Pip audit, test (3.12), test (3.13), and the required checks are test (3.12) and
test (3.13). A declined review therefore leaves no trace in CI; this registry is what makes
it visible to the triage queue.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change; measured over #111..#129, three PRs (#121, #123, #129) drew 'Review limit reached', so a decline that REFUSED would go red on real work and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. The dotfiles 'no complaints' review marker is deliberately NOT reused -- see the $comment on review_markers.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here — kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot] and dotfiles has 172. It is now OBSERVED HERE: measured 2026-10-12, the marker appears on 3 of the last 7 PRs (#171, #170, #167) and on none of the four Dependabot PRs, which the workflow skips. `## Incremental PR Reviewer Guide` is deliberately NOT declared: measured 2026-10-12, it appears on none of those 7. Declaring a marker WIDENS this gate, so an unobserved heading waits until the reworked workflow emits it (CI-001 PR2) rather than being copied from the SSOT, which is what this file's own rule forbids. The same login also posts release-please's 'Created releases' comment (#122); that text carries no marker, so it cannot attest.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked. Already in use here before this registry existed: #129 carries one.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #122 (chore(master): release 1.8.0): exactly these four paths, because release-please-config.json bumps the version in pyproject.toml and server.json under backend/ as well as writing the changelog there. Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch — the release PR is authored by github-actions[bot] here, the same login PR-Agent posts under, so an author rule would be ambiguous, and a branch rule would let any branch named to match walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
